purpose: Gate E execution/security qualification record for the pre-2.0 artifact. Every row names the executable test that asserts it and the negative case that would catch its removal. This record QUALIFIES author-side coverage; it does NOT discharge the independence requirement, which no author can supply.

components.question: Is the child-process approval surface incapable of self-approval?
components.negativeCase: WorkerApprovalPort throws at construction if a resolve/revoke/invalidate/mutate method appears; recordExecutionOutcome is scoped to the bound workerId.
components.note: DOWNGRADED to partial by independent review (D6, D7). The facade omits decision methods and pending consumption is rejected, but the constructor guard is verified by a VACUOUS test and the facade narrows an object without confining a process: a child can reopen ApprovalStore via import or the approval CLI. Treated as a narrowing, not an authority boundary.

components.question: Does a hard policy deny survive every session mode?
components.negativeCase: Deny stays deny across auto/bypass/ask; an allow is never invented; a consumed approval cannot be re-consumed; deny-wins when an allow and a deny both match.
components.note: REMEDIATED BUT NOT RE-REVIEWED, still NOT QUALIFIED. D1 is fixed (the ask-mode safe-shell bypass no longer bypasses a deny) and D11 is fixed (deny > ask > allow over all matching rules; the shipped defaults previously let a critical-risk capability read through an earlier allow). Both are mutation-checked. The clause cannot be claimed until an independent re-review confirms the fixes, and D3-D8 remain open.

components.question: Does an approval claimed and then crashed stay consumed rather than silently reusable?
components.negativeCase: A pending claim observed on replay is classified unverified and denied without reissuing authority; a legacy approval with no fingerprint fails closed and is re-asked; silence is never success.
components.note: DOWNGRADED to partial by independent review (D3, D4). Ordinary replay is genuinely asserted (denial, zero effects, consumed/unverified), but coordination replay creates a REPLACEMENT approval instead of denying uncertainty, and stale-lock takeover can admit two claimants.

components.question: Can a worker write outside its declared owned paths?
components.negativeCase: The owned-path rule decides every declared-scope write; a broader capability permission never widens the grant; file.create applies the router backstop to new files as well as overwrites. The bf29449b regression — gate returned the allow before the owned-path rule — is pinned by an explicit allow-listed-capability x session-mode table.
components.note: PARTIALLY REMEDIATED, still NOT QUALIFIED. D2 is fixed: a declared owned scope now denies unscopable mutation channels (shell, dynamic tools) via the `unscopable-mutation-rule` hard deny, mutation-checked by 4 tests in tests/policy/policy-gate.test.ts. Router backstop coverage for new files is still outside the cited evidence set, so the clause stays unqualified until that is added.

components.question: Are denied actions observably denied, and do they leave no side effect?
components.negativeCase: Protected paths are not written; a denied command is classified deny and does not reach dispatch; denial at the port and at dispatch level both produce a deny decision rather than an execution.
components.note: PARTIAL. Decision assertions exist and dispatch refusal is asserted for the paths below. REMOVED FROM EVIDENCE: tests/policy/command-classifier.test.ts — the classifier has NO production consumer (GitNexus risk UNKNOWN, confirmed by text search), so it classifies commands but proves nothing about denial or dispatch suppression. Citing it was a vacuous-evidence finding, now corrected. Full TUI operator-denial remains F-03.

independence.note: A model-independent review WAS obtained and it REJECTED the qualification. That is independence doing its job, not a clearance.

suiteRepair.found: 2026-10-24/25 during full-suite verification of this record.
suiteRepair.cause: Two fixtures configured model tiers under subagents.<tier>; createModelResolver reads config.models[tier]. getRoleModel threw "Subagent tier is unconfigured" and every assertion downstream of spawn() observed that error instead of the behaviour under test.
suiteRepair.scope: tests/agents/subagent-manager.test.ts (16) and tests/kernel/subagent-worker-executor.test.ts (4). Type-checking could not catch it: the projection is genuinely part of the type.
suiteRepair.fix: Fixtures now carry a real models block (default/fast/coding/thinking/critic).
suiteRepair.after: subagent-manager 19/19, subagent-worker-executor 13/13; node lane 8915 pass, 0 fail.
suiteRepair.preExisting: CONFIRMED pre-existing, not a regression: both suites fail identically at parent commit ea863a25 in a clean worktree.
suiteRepair.relevance: These are not Gate E evidence (the five clauses cite different files), but a suite that reports 20 failures cannot be read as green, so the repair is recorded here rather than left implicit.

independentReview.claim: Author-side qualification is NOT sound enough to accept as coverage of all five clauses.

iWasWrong: The author-side record claimed 5/5 clauses qualified. An independent review downgraded all five: authority and ownership are NOT QUALIFIED, F8b/crash-recovery/denied-action are partial. Two of the review's defects were in MY OWN validator (D9 forged independence, D10 HOLD exited 0) and both were reproduced by probe before fixing. The review also found a vacuous test whose claimed guard I verified by deletion: removing the constructor guard leaves all 14 tests green.

declaredGaps.gap: No explicit wrong-workspace test for the worker port
declaredGaps.why: The failure mode cannot be constructed through the port (no user-supplied workspace path), but the test itself does not exist

declaredGaps.gap: Tool-level operator denial not exercised through the full TUI scenario
declaredGaps.why: Denial is proven at port and dispatch level only
Prior evidence shows dependency serialization, not rejection of an unsynchronized conflict
Possible timing fragility in an approval test; one unreproduced observation

declaredGaps.gap: D4-04 delegate transport flake bounded, not fixed
declaredGaps.why: 42 consecutive passes, zero reproduction; a delegate case may not be the sole evidence for a baseline

fixed.what: Ask-mode safe-shell bypass now evaluates mandatory policy denies first. The probe uses this.root (not process.cwd()) and carries ownedPaths, so a scoped worker mutating "safe" command is caught. ToolResult shape corrected to {kind:"error",message} — the previous {kind:"error",error} plus a double cast rendered "Error: undefined". Also fixed isSafeShellCommand: `git branch -d x` was classified safe.

Inverted to an ALLOWLIST: owned-scope-channels.ts permits only tools whose targets are enumerable (file.create/file.delete/patch.apply) and reads mutability from ToolCapabilityRegistry.resolve(toolName).mutates. Everything else that mutates is denied for scoped workers. Covers shell, mcp.invoke, mcp__*, skill.create, agent.delegate, hook.create, coordination.run, schedule.propose. One module shared by PolicyGate and ToolExecutor.
fixed.test: tests/policy/policy-gate.test.ts — 8 channels x 3 session modes; reverting to the deny-list fails it

fixed.what: A consumed coordination binding is DENIED, and a lost claim race is denied, instead of minting a replacement approval.
fixed.test: tests/security/approval-consumed-propagation.test.ts — asserts deny, no replacement approvalId, and matchedRuleId; the tightening reproduced the defect before the fix

fixed.what: The validator now requires each run to carry the exact reproducible command referencing the files it claims ran, and requires component evidence to be a test or source file. A fabricated record (all-zero commit, IMAGINARY-RUNNER, package.json as evidence) is rejected.
fixed.test: benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.test.mjs — 2 tests fail when the checks are removed

fixed.what: Any HOLD exits non-zero, and the exit code is now asserted at the process level rather than only via outcome.

RuleEvaluator is deny>ask>allow over all matching rules (already fixed), AND a hard capability deny is now checked before the shell-whitelist ask branch, so a deny can no longer become an approval prompt.
fixed.test: tests/policy/rule-evaluator.test.ts (5 fail on revert) + policy-gate whitelist interaction

remediation.note: RE-COUNT after the 2026-10-25 two-axis review. The earlier claim of '4 of 11 closed' was OVERSTATED and is corrected here: D2 was partial (capability deny-list missed skill.create, agent.delegate, hook.create, coordination.run and dynamic mcp__*), and D11 was half-fixed (the evaluator precedence was fixed; the ask-before-hard-deny branch was not).
